correctness.rationale: The original positive-domain theorem is true: factorization of the marginal PGF gives the stated logarithmic coefficients, with the Poisson contribution only at j=1. The all-index endpoint estimate holds both when the beta kernel f_j(x)=x^j(1-x) is monotone on [q^2,q] and when it is maximized there; in the latter case the two endpoints each exceed half its maximum by the two displayed exact ratios. Thus w_j=a_j-a_(j+1)>0 even at alpha=0,1 and lambda=0. I separately checked the original unrelated-rate failure: at survival ratios 1/6 and 5/6 the numerator factor is 1-(13/18)z and a_3-a_2=35/5832. For the repaired claim, differentiating along phi_t(z)=1-e^(-t)+e^(-t)z gives the telescoping series sum_j w_j(1-phi_t(z)^j); integrating its negative yields the log innovation quotient. Expanding each power binomially gives nonnegative rates with total at most (-log c)a_1. The ell=j term supplies the strictly positive lower bound w_j(1-c^j)/j; factoring each affine substitution gives exactly the claimed closed rates. The worked positive-domain signed partial fractions are checked by the residues at 2, 4 and 19/4 and the limiting constant 2/5. In particular the coefficient of G_(1/4) is -3/10. At the negative witness r=-4/11 and the second canonical increase is -11/64+240/1331=719/85184; differentiating the z^2 coefficient at t=0 gives its negative and rules out an innovation for sufficiently small positive t. These are exact analytic checks, not assertions inferred from a grid. The replacement is in /workspace/repairs/1; its verification program is an optional standard-library replay and was not used to establish the infinite claims. The frozen script was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: This PASS is for the substantive corrective result in the replacement, not for the advertised originality of the frozen claim. The frozen claim does not pass as a new existence assertion: Ghodake et al. (2025), Definition 1 and Eqs. (6)–(10), already posit the transmuted-geometric marginal itself for binomial INAR thinning with unrestricted retention in [0,1), and give precisely the same required PGF quotient. Specialize to their positive transmutation domain and take season one; convolving an independent Poisson just adds a Poisson innovation of rate lambda(1-c). Crucially, the earlier assertion is not an established proof of positivity: its geometric-mixture interpretation gives a negative weight at a positive interior parameter point, and its unrestricted negative-range construction fails. The separate replacement identifies that substantive gap, proves validity throughout the nonnegative range, and provides the strictly positive compound-Poisson innovation rates, including an explicitly nonnegative construction where the older signed decomposition cannot certify anything. Neither the erroneous mixture interpretation nor the general discrete criterion gives that positive-domain verification by specialization. No novelty is attributed to the signed PGF quotient, the underlying model, the general criterion, or the distinct same-day negative-domain classification.
residual_risks: The earlier positive existence assertion is verified; no first-assertion claim is made. Another lawful, published correction or explicit proof of positivity may exist outside the inspected passages and bounded searches.

The corrective novelty is not the generic log-ratio representation itself; it is the model-specific proof of positivity and the precise separation of the signed-decomposition error from true negative-domain nonexistence.

value.rationale: The repaired result addresses a real model-existence issue, rather than renaming the old quotient or inferring probability weights from a formal rational identity. It yields a valid positive simulation representation for every retention and jump size throughout the nonnegative transmutation range and a concrete interior case where the published geometric-mixture reading fails although existence is true. The second example distinguishes that proof error from actual nonexistence when negative transmutation is allowed. The repair is independently useful for fixed-marginal count autoregressions even with no claim of full negative-range classification or novelty of the original existence statement.
